title: Add throughput-style SLI (rate over window) + error budget reporting by tier
author: Aisha Bello
release_notes: SLO toolkit now supports throughput/rate SLIs (e.g., tokens/sec) and can report error budgets segmented by tier for Dedicated deployments.
description:
Summary: This PR extends slo-toolkit to support throughput-style SLIs (rate-over-window) and error budget reporting grouped by tier. This unblocks the Dedicated throughput SLO work (tokens/sec) where the objective is expressed as a sustained rate measured over a rolling window rather than a simple availability ratio.

Background / motivation: Our existing SLO model assumes a classic good/total request ratio. Dedicated throughput SLOs are defined in terms of sustained output tokens/sec with explicit tier semantics (Standard/Performance/Premium). We need (1) a first-class way to compute rate SLIs over a window and (2) the ability to emit error budget + burn summaries per tier (and optionally per deployment_id) to match customer packaging/contract language.

Key changes: 1) New SLI kind: rate_over_window - Adds a new SLI type that evaluates a PromQL expression as a rate over a configurable evaluation window (e.g., 5m) and then compares it against an objective threshold. - Supports optional normalization labels (e.g., model) and mandatory grouping dimensions when requested (e.g., tier). - Handles missing data explicitly (configurable: treat as 'no data' vs 'bad') to avoid silently passing when metrics drop.

2) Error budget reporting by tier - Adds grouping support in the reporter so a single SLO definition can produce multiple series and summaries by label value. - Adds CLI/report output to show error budget remaining + burn rate per tier (and aggregate) for the same SLO.

3) Config schema + validation - Adds schema validation for throughput SLO definitions: requires objective to be in units consistent with the query (toolkit cannot fully verify units, but we validate presence of unit hints and required labels). - Adds guardrails for cardinality: warns when grouping by deployment_id without also scoping down the query.

4) Docs + examples - Adds an example throughput SLO config for Dedicated, including tier segmentation. - Documents how to map runtime metrics to the toolkit (expects the upstream metric already aggregated to 'tokens per second' or computable via rate()).

Example config (new): kind: rate_over_window name: dedicated-throughput-tokens-per-sec service: inference/dedicated sli: query: "sum by (tier) (rate(redwood_inference_output_tokens_total{mode=\"dedicated\"}[5m]))" window: "5m" group_by: ["tier"] no_data: "fail" objective: "1200" unit: "tokens/sec" alerting: burn_rates: - name: "fast" window: "1h" threshold: "14" - name: "slow" window: "6h" threshold: "6"

Implementation notes: - Internally, we model rate_over_window as a threshold SLO with a computed SLI time series. The evaluator requests samples over the evaluation period, applies the windowed query, and compares each sample to the objective to compute 'bad time' minutes. - Reporter now supports 'group_by' and will produce one error budget per group value. To keep output stable, groups are sorted and capped by a max_groups setting (default 25) with a warning when exceeded.

Files / modules touched (high level): - pkg/config/schema.go: extend config schema + validation for rate_over_window and group_by - pkg/eval/rate_sli.go: new evaluator for rate SLIs (window handling, no_data policy) - pkg/report/report.go: add grouping + per-tier summaries - cmd/sloctl/report.go: CLI output changes to render grouped budgets - docs/sli-kinds.md + examples/dedicated-throughput-by-tier.yaml: documentation + example

CI / testing: - Added unit tests for rate_sli evaluator (window parsing, missing data policy, threshold comparison). - Added golden tests for grouped report rendering (ensures stable ordering and max_groups behavior). - All existing suites pass.

Rollout / compatibility: - Backwards compatible: existing SLO configs continue to work unchanged. - New config keys: sli.kind=rate_over_window, sli.window, group_by, no_data, unit. - This PR does not ship new metrics; it assumes runtime/gateway export labels include tier (see redwood PR for metric emission).

Links: - Linear: ENG-2194 (instrument throughput SLI metrics), ENG-2201 (dashboards/alerts for Dedicated throughput) - Related: Redwood runtime metric emission + labels (tier/model/region) and Grafana dashboards PRs.

Review notes / open questions: - Objective is a string in config today; we parse as float64. This keeps schema stable but is mildly odd. If we want typed units, we can do that in a follow-up without blocking Dedicated SLO launch. - We currently treat 'no data' as configurable but default to warn+fail for rate SLIs. Please sanity check against SRE expectations.

Conversation highlights: Rafael Mendes: Can we ensure missing metrics don’t silently pass? We’ve been burned by that. Aisha Bello (author): Yes, rate_over_window defaults to no_data=fail (explicit) and tests cover it. Also added a warning when a query returns empty series for an entire evaluation interval.

Sergio Costa: Grouping by tier is great; do we cap group count? We don’t want someone grouping by deployment_id and exploding the report. Aisha Bello (author): Added max_groups=25 default with override, plus validation warning when group_by includes high-cardinality labels without a selector on deployment_id.

Logan Wright: Do we require the tier label? Aisha Bello (author): Toolkit doesn’t enforce tier globally; it enforces that group_by labels exist in the query output. Dedicated configs will include tier. Added docs callout that upstream emission must include tier.

Miles Thornton: The burn rate alert windows in the example look like availability SLOs. Does the math still work for throughput? Aisha Bello (author): Yes; we still compute bad-time minutes based on threshold breach. Burn rate is error-budget consumption rate over time window, independent of what the SLI measures.

Approvals: - Rafael Mendes approved after adding no_data=fail default and a warning when group count exceeds cap. - Sergio Costa approved after golden test updates for stable report formatting.

Merge: Squash merged into main.
